questions.q: When two compounds ${ACl}_{3}$ and ${DCl}_{3}$ of two elements $A$ and $D$ are mixed together, a compound ${ADCl}_{6}$ is formed. The structural analysis showed that ${ADCl}_{6}$ is an ionic compound. Given that ${DCl}_{3}$ is trigonal planar and ${ACl}_{3}$ is trigonal pyramidal, predict the shape of the cation if the shape of the anion is tetrahedral.
questions.solution:
⇒& Since, ${DCl}_{3}$ is trigonal planar, hence, $' D '$ belongs to the boron family.

⇒ Since~${ACl}_{3}$~is trigonal pyramidal, hence, $' A '$ belongs to the nitrogen family.

⇒~${DCl}_{3} + {ACl}_{3} \to \left[{DCl}_{2}\right] +\left[{ACl}_{4}\right] -$~or~\left[{ACl}_{2}\right] +\left[{DCl}_{4}\right] -$

If the anionic part is \left[{ACl}_{4}\right] -$ which has a see-saw structure, then, cationic part will be \left[{DCl}_{2}\right] +$ where~the hybridization of $D$ will be $sp$ and hence, the shape will be linear.

If the anionic part is \left[{DCl}_{4}\right] -$ i.e., it is of tetrahedral shape, then, the cationic part will be \left[{ACl}_{2}\right] +$ which will be bent with ${sp}^{2}$ hybridisation.

$

questions.q: If the electronegativity of& $C, H, O, N$and~$S$~are~$2 . 5, 2 . 1, 3 . 5, 3 . 0$~and~$2 . 5$,& respectively, then the correct order of polarity of bonds is:
options: $S - O > C - N > O - H > C - H$
$S - O > C - N > C - H > O - H$
$O - H > S - O > C - N > C - H$
$C - N > C - H > O - H > S - O$
questions.solution:
Electronegativity of atoms forming a bond& is& used to determine whether, the& given& bond& will be non-polar covalent, polar& covalent& or ionic.

It is the ability of an atom in a particular molecule to attract electrons to itself& (the greater the value of $EN$, the greater the force of attraction by atom~on~electrons).

If~electronegativity difference is more, there is more charge separation and thus, bond is more polar.

The electronegativity difference between:

\left(i\right)$ Sulphur and Oxygen$= 1$

\left(ii\right)$ Carbon and Nitrogen$= 0 . 5$

\left(iii\right)$ Oxygen and Hydrogen$= 1 . 4$

\left(iv\right)$ Carbon and Hydrogen$= 0 . 4$

So, the correct order of the polarity of bonds is:

$O - H > S - O > C - N > C - H$

questions.q: The $\text{N} - \text{N}$ bond length in ${N}_{2} \text{O}$ is $1 .12 Å$, slightly longer than a typical~$\text{N} ≡ \text{N}$~bond and the $\text{N} - \text{O}$ bond length is $1 .19 Å$, slightly shorter than a typical $\text{N} - \text{O}$ bond.
options: ${ \begin{cases}\text{N} - \text{N} & \text{bond order less than 3} \\ \text{N} - \text{O} & \text{bond order more than 1}\end{cases}$
${ \begin{cases}\text{N} - \text{N} & \text{bond order greater than 3} \\ \text{N} - \text{O} & \text{bond order less than 1}\end{cases}$
${ \begin{cases}\text{N} - \text{N} & \text{bond order less than 1} \\ \text{N} - \text{O} & \text{bond order greater than 1}\end{cases}$
questions.solution:
Bond order is defined as the number of bonds present between two bonding atoms in a molecule or compound.& In general, the bond order of $N ≡ N$~is 3, and that of $N - O$~is $1$. Bond length and bond order are inversely proportional to each other. If bond order increases, the bond length decreases, and if bond order decreases, the bond length increases.~

~

Bond length~follows the order :

$TripleBond < DoubleBond < SingleBond$

~

The ${N}_{2}O$ molecule exhibits the phenomenon of resonance as shown below:

~

Due to the above resonance phenomenon, the bond order of $N - N$ bond becomes $2$~(less than $3$) and hence, the bond is slightly longer $( 1 .12 Å )$~than a normal $N ≡ N$ bond.

~

On the other hand, the bond order of $N - O$ is also~$2$~(greater~than $1$)~due to the resonance phenomenon. Hence,~the bond length is slightly shorter~$( 1 .19 Å )$~ than the typical $N - O$ single bond.

questions.q: $Sb{F}_{3}$ reacts with $Xe{F}_{4}$ and $Xe{F}_{6}$ to form ionic compounds  \left[Xe{F}_{3}^{+}\right] \left[Sb{F}_{6}^{-}\right]$ and  \left[$Xe{F}_{5}^{+}\right] \left[$Sb{F}_{6}^{-}\right]$ then molecular shape of  \left[Xe{F}_{3}^{+}\right]$ ion and  \left[$Xe{F}_{5}^{+}\right]$ ion respectively$
questions.solution:
The shapes of these ions are as follows

$[ Xe{F}_{3}^{+} ] :$ ~Bent-T shape ( $sp^{3}d$ -hybridisation)

$[ Xe{F}_{5}^{+} ] :$ ~Square pyramidal ( $sp^{3}d^{2}$ -hybridisation)

questions.q: How many of the following species are diamagnetic? $\mathrm{He}}_{2}^{+}, \mathrm{H}}_{2}, $\mathrm{H}}_{2}^{+}, \mathrm{H}}_{2}^{-}, $\mathrm{He}$
questions.solution: According to molecular orbital theory, species with all paired electrons in their electronic configuration are diamagnetic in nature. $\mathrm{He}_2^{+} \rightarrow$ Has total 3 electrons, thus it contains one unpaired electron and is paramagnetic in nature. $\mathrm{H}_2 \rightarrow$ Has total 2 electrons, thus it contains all paired electrons and is diamagnetic in nature. $\mathrm{H}_2^{+} \rightarrow$ Has only l electron, thus it is paramagnetic in nature. $\mathrm{H}_2^{-} \rightarrow$ Has total 3 electrons, thus it contains one unpaired electron and is paramagnetic in nature. $\mathrm{He} \rightarrow$ Contains total two (2) electrons and has no unpaired electron, thus is diamagnetic in nature. Hence, among the given species, we have only two of them which are diamagnetic and thus, option (2) is the correct answer.

questions.q: Compare& ${ZnCl}_{2}$~and~${MgCl}_{2}$~and find~which is more soluble in organic solvents? (atomic number of~$Zn = 30$~and that of~$Mg = 12$& )&
questions.solution:
As we know that according to solubility rule : Like dissolves like means.

Polar dissolves with& polar and non-polar dissolves with& non-polar.

Ionic compounds are more polar as compared to covalent compound and water acts as best polar solvent& in which ionic compound will be more soluble in water or in aqueous medium.

According to like dissolve like concept, more covalent is more soluble in organic solvent.

So,& ${ZnCl}_{2}$~is more covalent as MgCl2.

~Size :~${r}_{Mg^{+ 2}} > {r}_{Zn^{+ 2}}$

questions.q: Given below are two statements Assertion (A): Ionic compounds are formed by nondirectional bonds Reasoning (R): They are soluble in nonpolar solvents The correct answer is
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of $(A)$
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of $(A)$
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution: Ionic bonds are electrostatic forces of attraction that are non-directional in nature. Thus, (A) is correct. Ionic compounds are soluble in polar solvents that solvate them via ion-dipole interactions. Thus, $(\mathrm{R})$ is incorrect.
